statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ front-month trades near 29,561 (+0.14%) and has eased back into the lower half of the 29,530.50-29,682.50 band, roughly 0.51% wide, that has now contained about fourteen hours of trade with the session high still unretested. Tail holds at 5 because that path is contained and two-way. Stress ticks up to 56: Brent has extended to about $97.41 (+1.2%) after printing a six-week high of $97.05 earlier today, while WTI is near $92.21 (+0.8%), and the energy strength is not transmitting to index futures. US cash equity, Treasury and Cboe markets are closed for Labor Day, CME equity index futures halt at 17:00 UTC and restart at 22:00 UTC, and the flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covers the European cash close running into that halt.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and Tail remains far below the block threshold in every hour of this outlook. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the shortened Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily at the 22:00 UTC restart that opens the Tuesday trade date after five closed hours. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The elevated Stress reading describes a difficult but recoverable environment and does not by itself change the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a fourteen-hour band through the Labor Day session as Brent extends past $97.40 and US cash markets stay shut
body:
The observed price path remains the strongest evidence this hour and it continues to argue for a low tail value. The band from 29,530.50 to 29,682.50, about 0.51% wide, has now contained roughly fourteen hours of trade. NQ is near 29,561, up 0.14% on a 29,535.25 open, and has drifted from the 29,637 and 29,618 prints of the previous two hours back into the lower half of that band. The session high was made early, rejected, and has still not been retested. Containment with working retracements is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency that overwhelms a mean-reversion approach.

Energy is the one input that has genuinely moved this hour. Brent is about $97.41, up roughly 1.2% on the day, having printed $97.05 earlier as a six-week high and then extended above it; WTI is near $92.21, up about 0.8%. Trading Economics reported Brent fluctuating above $96 after last week's 9.3% surge, with the US destroying an Iranian oil tanker in retaliation for ballistic missile strikes on Navy vessels and Tehran threatening a restricted maritime zone, while US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the naval blockade would continue but commercial passage remains secure. That is a genuine escalation in the energy complex. It matters here mainly because it is not transmitting: equity futures are flat to slightly lower against an oil market printing new session highs.

Cross-asset alignment is therefore absent, which is itself informative. Asia-Pacific closed sharply higher on memory-chip strength, with the Nikkei 225 up 2.1% to 66,399.84 and the Kospi up 4.6% to 6,995.39, Samsung Electronics +5.7% and SK Hynix +8.1%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 0.9%. Europe is mixed and small: the CAC 40 up less than 0.1% at 8,282.06, the DAX down 0.2% at 25,993.23 and the FTSE 100 down 0.2% at 10,814.01. US index futures disperse rather than align, with Dow futures down about 0.3% and S&P 500 futures little changed. VIX last printed near 15.17 before the Cboe holiday closure. US cash Treasuries are shut, so the H.15 curve as of 3 September, with the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.25%, is the latest available reference and cannot move today. Divergence of this kind normally lifts uncertainty rather than tail risk, and that is how it is scored.

The macro backdrop is what keeps Stress in the mid-fifties. The week carries NFIB and a 3-year auction on Tuesday, a 10-year auction on Wednesday, PPI and jobless claims on Thursday at 12:30 UTC, and CPI with preliminary Michigan sentiment on Friday, ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC. None of that can print today. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 06:39 UTC and is now roughly five hours old, beyond the freshness bar, so it is treated as stale supporting material only; its non-aligned reading of index, rates and energy futures is consistent with the independent evidence above but is not relied upon.

Confidence is held at 85. Live NQ pricing, oil, the verified geopolitical sequence, the Asian and European closes and the seven-day US calendar are all in hand. The gaps that remain, live US cash equity, Treasury and volatility prints, are structural holiday closures rather than evidential weakness, and the closures themselves are verified fact.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday afternoon, stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk, eased to 6 and then 5 once that restart proved orderly, lifted to 7 as the overnight high extended, and settled back to 6 and then 5 for the last three hours as that high was retraced and left unretested. Every available hour mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress ranged from 54 to 60, peaking at 60 into the Sunday close before easing into the mid-fifties across the Asian and European hours. Confidence sat between 84 and 86 throughout. The dominant mode was normal in every available hour, and no hour in the window produced observed persistent one-way structure.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the rest of the European morning and a holiday afternoon traded against closed US cash equity, Treasury and Cboe markets, a shortened futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, and the Tuesday Asian session into the European cash open. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 5 for the current hour and the next, 6 across the late European morning and the holiday afternoon where thinned depth meets no US cash backstop, 8 in the flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European close into the halt, 5 through the five closed hours where no price path can form, 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart for concentrated gap repricing, and 6 to 7 across the Tuesday Asian session and the European cash open into the 10:00 UTC NFIB release. Stress runs from 50 during the halt to 58 in the flagged window, and Confidence decays from 85 to 71 with horizon. Every hour maps to EA_ON and green, and the dominant mode stays normal throughout because no observed evidence supports a directional or event-driven label.
